youtube.baslik: What do you check before approving an automated audiogram? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: In automated audiometry, an algorithm runs the threshold-finding steps, and at the end of the test quality warnings are produced along with the thresholds. Before approving, look not only at the thresholds but also at these warnings: if there are many button presses with no sound, or false alarms, if background noise exceeded the limit, or if there is a masking warning, the result is not considered reliable. If in doubt, the relevant frequencies are retested manually; automated results are not used for diagnostic decisions without an audiologist's review.

Before approving an automated audiogram, check quality warnings, not just thresholds.
Button presses with no sound, called false alarms, are counted.
With many false alarms, excess noise or masking warnings, distrust the result.
If in doubt, retest those frequencies manually; this prevents a wrong report.
